notes.title: Patch 1.1.3
notes.notes:
Patch 1.1.3 is a tiny update, with a single fix: 

 Fixed a matchmaking bug that sometimes caused players to be kicked out of lobbies for no reason, right before starting a match.

notes.title: Patch 1.1.2b
notes.notes:
Patch 1.1.2b addresses a few bugs and other issues brought up by the community:

 (Hopefully) Fixed an issue that would sometimes cause an infinite loop of merging lobbies during matchmaking.
 Fixed a bug where the game became unresponsive for about a minute if you opened the in-game menu as the match finished.
 Fixed poor performance when using one of the blockers from the gear pack.
 Fixed MMR not being properly taken into account when sorting players into teams.
 Improved main menu readability.
 Reduced max held energy for solo Reactor Rush and Point-to-Point rounds to match the reactor target.
 Exiting the post-game screen now also exits matchmaking. Button label has been updated to reflect the change.

notes.title: Patch 1.1.1c
notes.notes:
Patch 1.1.1c adds a handful of tweaks that didn't make it into the 1.1 Update:

 Refreshed lighting in the main level
 Added timer indicators to warn about the end of the round
 Improved map selection for small lobbies
 Filled some holes in the map that let you escape into the abyss
 Fixed some loading backgrounds showing bright artifacts at lower quality levels
 Fixed some misplaced visual effects on control points and reactors
 Reduced pistol damage:[expand type=details]
 Previous: 40/45/50/55/60
 New: 32/36/40/44/48
[/expand] Rebalanced shotgun damage:[expand type=details]
 Previous: 96/108/120/132/144
 New: 99/108/117/126/135
 Shotguns also now do 25% less damage to blockers.
[/expand]

notes.title: Update 1.1
notes.notes:
Hello patch-notes-readers, and thanks for joining us on our first update since  1.0 Release! The team here at Moonray Studios been keeping busy since we last spoke, with a major weapon rebalance, a few new features, and lots of bugfixes. Let's dive in!

The biggest change you'll notice in 1.1 is the weapon rebalance:

 Weapons have been rescaled overall: Legendary weapons are mostly unchanged, but Common weapons have been buffed significantly, now performing at the level of the old rare weapons. Uncommon, Rare, and Epic weapons have been rescaled accordingly.
 You'll now only ever spawn with Common weapons (which are much better than they used to be).
 Weapons spawned around the world will always be Uncommon or better.
  All weapons now come in every rarity. [expand type=details]In practice this means we have added 10 new weapons:

 Epic/Legendary Pistol
 Legendary Shotgun
 Common/Uncommon Sniper
 Common/Uncommon Thumper
 Common/Uncommon/Rare Carpet
[/expand] Sniper damage has been rebalanced, and you can no longer one-shot enemies with no shield unless you get a headshot: 
[expand type=details]
 Previous: ~/~/100/115/130, with 2x headshot damage: ~/~/200/235/260
 New: 40/50/60/70/80, with 3x headshot damage: 120/150/180/210/240
[/expand] The Carpet, Thumper, and Torpedo now do bonus damage to blockers.
You might also notice a new "Tournament Password" dropdown on the main menu, which you can use to set up larger private matches. By entering a password here, you'll only make matches with other lobbies using that password. For custom matches, each team should party up, and then when ready, you can enter a password to only matchmake with other teams using that password. This ensures your party won't be split up by the matchmaker.

Some other changes in 1.1:

 Reduced total size on disk and further optimized RAM & VRAM usage.
 Added option in key bindings menu to reset to default bindings.
 Tweaked MMR values to make it a little more dynamic, i.e. each match should contribute more to your overall rating.
And as always, we took the time to squash some more bugs:

 Fixed an issue that made the in-game menu sometimes inaccessible on controller.
 Fixed a longstanding visual bug when the other team quits a match, which would then show a "Round 2" or similar loading screen to remaining players during the post-game sequence.
 Fixed an issue where some text, including the tutorial, would not display when your system language is not set to English.
 Fixed a matchmaking bug that would sometimes cause a lobby merge failure.
 Removed bloom from the UI so it no longer feels like you're reading in a swimming pool.
 Fixed some UI Elements that were too blurry at lower quality settings.
Of course, the biggest problem we've been hearing from players is that they're having trouble finding a match. Unfortunately, that's one bug we're not currently able to fix via patch notes, but we do have a solution: Starting this weekend, we're introducing our Saturday Night Dives: Every Saturday, we have 3 dedicated times for you to dive in and meet up with other players for a match. We've tried to spread them out to cover our fans in different time zones. 
Of course, you can enjoy Tidal Shock any day, any time if you bring a friend. (and why not? it's free after all!) Plus, you can always look for a game with the fine folks over on our Discord Server.

That's all for now! Dive into the arena and check out the update for yourself!
🌊⚡

notes.title: Tidal Shock 1.0 Content Update
notes.notes:
With the launch of Tidal Shock: Off the Hook 1.0, we’re not just bringing new modes, visuals, and chaos to the arena — We’re also bringing the fight to your hands. 
We have released our Steam Deck–Ready native Linux build. It’s optimized, controller-tuned, and tested to run smooth — whether you’re docked, handheld, or somewhere in between.

We didn’t design for Deck on day one — but once we saw what this little machine could do, we knew we had to make a build for it.
✅ Native Linux version
✅ Full controller support
✅ Smooth performance and fast loads
✅ 360° underwater chaos that just feels right in your hands

If you’re a Steam Deck player, we built this for you. This isn’t just a game that runs — it thrives.
And we’re hoping your feedback helps push it toward full Verified status.

🎮 Practice in Solo Mode.
🛠️ Warm up in Private Matches.
💥 Ride torpedoes anywhere you want.
The ocean is open — and now it fits in your backpack.

notes.title: Version 1.0 Is Now Live!
notes.notes:
🌊 The wait is over. 🌊

After a long, scrappy ride through Early Access, we’re happy to announce that Tidal Shock: Off the Hook 1.0 releases today — and we've got a whole host of changes for you, so let's dive right in!

A little over a month ago, we started quietly making some big updates while we prepared for our full release. In case you missed it, here's the gist:

 We took Tidal Shock off the hook - it's now free to play! (And never pay-to-win - the only things you can buy are cosmetics.)
 We added all-new game modes: Depthmatch, Control, and Point-To-Point on top of our classic Reactor Rush mode, and each match is now a three-round burst of different modes across different parts of the Tidal Shock Arena!
 We expanded the map and now support matches of up to 12 players, plus team matches (we were sick of free-for-all too).
 We added over 50 achievements! (and there are even more today - see below!)
 We added Rankings, XP & Awards for unlocking prestige skins, and an MMR system to find other players at your skill level.
 We gave the whole game a makeover, from the map to the characters to the HUD.
 We added new skins to unlock, and premium skins to buy, including the Gear Pack, finally letting you ride in style. 
 We made tons of rebalances, performance improvements, and bugfixes.
 Plus, every week we hosted events and DLC giveaways!
But that's not what this announcement is about - today we're releasing Tidal Shock 1.0, our full release out of early access, including a ton of new content:

 The long-requested and long-awaited tutorial is finally here (optional of course). No more dropping into your first match with a pro while you're still learning how to use the torpedo. Because also releasing today are...
 Private matches! You won't earn XP or achievements, but now you can dive in with friends for a grudge match or to learn the ropes with a buddy. You can also hop in solo get a feel for the arena at your own pace.
 If in-game tutorials aren't your style, we also have a short Player's Guide Video to get you up to speed.
 The map has expanded once more - There's a whole new area to explore (the minefield), plus some major changes inside the existing map that we hope will shake things up for those who have it memorized.
 We're also launching our native linux build today! Steam deck users in particular should notice a significant performance increase. Check it out!
 And finally, we're releasing 7 new achievements today, each focused on mastering every weapon in the game:

🛡️ Not So Fast
🛡️ Hail Mary
🛡️ Sharpshooter
🛡️ Splash Damage
🛡️ Nowhere To Hide
🛡️ Spray and Pray
🛡️ Fish In a Barrel
In celebration of our release, we're also running a launch week sale: All Character Packs are 15% off! On top of that we're releasing two new bundles for those who want to Dip Their Toes, or even take a Deep Dive into Moonray Studios' back-catalog, pairing some sweet Tidal Shock Character Packs with our last game, Debris - Tidal Shock's narrative-driven older sibling, for a fraction of the price! Check them out now!

❤️ From Us to You
We’re a tiny indie team. We built this on guts, glowsticks, and way too much caffeine.
We couldn’t have done it without your feedback, chaos, and love.
If you’re enjoying the ride, leave a review, and tell your friends! Tidal Shock has been a labor of love, and more than anything we would love to keep improving and updating Tidal Shock for you guys.

Thank you for the support. We hope you enjoy playing the game as much as we've loved making it.

🌊See you in the arena!
[Play Now] | [Join the Discord]

notes.title: Patch 0.4.18c
notes.notes:
This patch enables the Full Throttle Event!

More details:

 Control has been simplified - instead of multiple sub-rounds, the control point will move around the map whenever a single team manages to score 50 points at that location. First to 100 points wins! 

 Overall this shouldn't affect the gameplay significantly, except in close three-player matches where you'll be likely to see a fourth control point pop up.
 This mostly just aligns the game mode's architecture with other existing modes, and makes end-game scoring simpler to understand.
 You now get a kill if a player suicides within 5 seconds of you damaging them. 

With this change in mind, we've also removed the -1 point penalty for suicide in Depthmatch.
 Refreshed UI:

 All text should now be legible when played on a handheld or TV.
 Simplified weapon display on HUD to make rarities easier to understand.
 Added reorient and menu control display to the main HUD. As always, these can be turned off in the settings menu.
 Added support for Cyrillic and other characters in players' usernames.

notes.title: Patch 0.4.17a

This patch enables the Power Play Event.

🌊 Dive in and check it out!

notes.title: Patch 0.4.16b
notes.notes:
A bit of a mish-mash of bug fixes, cleanup and gameplay tweaks this time:

 Fixed an issue when other players quit the match while you were still loading in, that manifested in a few ways:

 Sometimes you'd get stuck on the loading screen
 Sometimes you'd get into the match alone without disconnecting automatically
 Sometimes you'd be pushed back to the main menu, but with weird lighting and have trouble rejoining the queue
 Sometimes you'd make it back to the menu, but then when you tried to play again you'd be kicked out of the match, with in-game HUD and lots of other visual craziness
  Fixed the matchmaker sometimes mixing up which players should go on which team, in particular brand new players getting paired up against players who had played a lot, but had lost a few games recently.
 Increased torpedo damage from 80 to 125 - it should have no trouble plowing through enemy blockers now!

 Self-damage also slightly increased from 20 to 25
  Removed a bunch of old content that's no longer in use, shrinking the install size a bit and hopefully also improving performance a little.

🌊Hop in and check it out!

Hop in and check it out!

notes.title: Patch 0.1.14f
notes.notes:
This patch makes significant improvements to our controller support, which has had some nasty bugs since our free-to-play transition.

The following fixes are included:

 All menus are now navigable entirely with the controller.
 Settings menu has a new layout that is much more controller-friendly.
 You'll no longer be navigating the in-game menu in the background while playing - an issue that sometimes caused you to open settings pages or even quit the game accidentally!
 Torpedo is now useable on controller no matter what your base sensitivity is.
 You'll no longer drop a blocker when resuming on controller in the in-game menu.
 Improved UI navigation speed on controller.

Other Misc. Fixes:

 Fixed an issue where sometimes the game would crash as you were trying to quit.
 (Hopefully!) Fixed an issue where temp graphics would sometimes show up when loading into a match.

notes.title: Patch 0.4.14c

Some additional bugfixes:


 12-player matches should no longer kick out 4 players randomly
 No longer incorrectly showing some players as disconnected on the post-game screen

notes.title: Patch 0.4.13e
notes.notes:
You may have noticed Tidal Shock was running a little slow...

In our excitement to deliver so much new content with our Off The Hook Update, we may have neglected some performance considerations. This update addresses them in a few ways:

 We've added a quality dropdown to the settings menu with 7 presets ranging from Minimum to Ultra, to handle machines of all shapes and sizes (but we're begging you not to use minimum quality... it makes the artists cry). 
 Across all quality settings, you should see a small performance boost from some overall cleanup we've done. Most noticeably, it shouldn't be hoarding RAM (sometimes up to 14GB) and VRAM (sometimes up to 7GB!) like it used to. 

Our lead dev claims that you could play the game with under 4GB RAM and 1GB VRAM now, but we don't have a machine like that to test on, so decide for yourself if you want to believe him. If he's wrong, feel free to give him hell on the #tidalshock-bugs channel on Discord.

One more thing! The first time you launch after this update, a quality setting will be picked automatically for you, but that's just a guess at which setting will run well on your machine - hop in a match and switch settings on the fly to see what works best for you!

🌊 See you in the arena!
